NKJV.1: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, And princes will rule with justice.
NKJV.2: A man will be as a hiding place from the wind, And a cover from the tempest, As rivers of water in a dry place, As the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
NKJV.3: The eyes of those who see will not be dim, And the ears of those who hear will listen.
NKJV.4: Also the heart of the rash will understand knowledge, And the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.
NKJV.5: The foolish person will no longer be called generous, Nor the miser said to be bountiful;
NKJV.6: For the foolish person will speak foolishness, And his heart will work iniquity: To practice ungodliness, To utter error against the LORD, To keep the hungry unsatisfied, And he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
NKJV.7: Also the schemes of the schemer are evil; He devises wicked plans To destroy the poor with lying words, Even when the needy speaks justice.
NKJV.8: But a generous man devises generous things, And by generosity he shall stand.
NKJV.9: Rise up, you women who are at ease, Hear my voice; You complacent daughters, Give ear to my speech.
NKJV.10: In a year and some days You will be troubled, you complacent women; For the vintage will fail, The gathering will not come.
NKJV.11: Tremble, you women who are at ease; Be troubled, you complacent ones; Strip yourselves, make yourselves bare, And gird sackcloth on your waists.
NKJV.12: People shall mourn upon their breasts For the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
NKJV.13: On the land of my people will come up thorns and briers, Yes, on all the happy homes in the joyous city;
NKJV.14: Because the palaces will be forsaken, The bustling city will be deserted. The forts and towers will become lairs forever, A joy of wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks—
NKJV.15: Until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high, And the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, And the fruitful field is counted as a forest.
NKJV.16: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, And righteousness remain in the fruitful field.
NKJV.17: The work of righteousness will be peace, And the effect of righteousness, quietness and assurance forever.
NKJV.18: My people will dwell in a peaceful habitation, In secure dwellings, and in quiet resting places,
NKJV.19: Though hail comes down on the forest, And the city is brought low in humiliation.
NKJV.20: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, Who send out freely the feet of the ox and the donkey.

NASB.1: Behold, a king will reign righteously And princes will rule justly.
NASB.2: Each will be like a refuge from the wind And a shelter from the storm, Like streams of water in a dry country, Like the shade of a huge rock in a parched land.
NASB.3: Then the eyes of those who see will not be blinded, And the ears of those who hear will listen.
NASB.4: The mind of the hasty will discern the truth, And the tongue of the stammerers will hasten to speak clearly.
NASB.5: No longer will the fool be called noble, Or the rogue be spoken of [as] generous.
NASB.6: For a fool speaks nonsense, And his heart inclines toward wickedness: To practice ungodliness and to speak error against the LORD, To keep the hungry person unsatisfied And to withhold drink from the thirsty.
NASB.7: As for a rogue, his weapons are evil; He devises wicked schemes To destroy [the] afflicted with slander, Even though [the] needy one speaks what is right.
NASB.8: But the noble man devises noble plans; And by noble plans he stands.
NASB.9: Rise up, you women who are at ease, [And] hear my voice; Give ear to my word, You complacent daughters.
NASB.10: Within a year and [a few] days You will be troubled, O complacent [daughters]; For the vintage is ended, [And] the [fruit] gathering will not come.
NASB.11: Tremble, you [women] who are at ease; Be troubled, you complacent [daughters]; Strip, undress and put [sackcloth] on [your] waist,
NASB.12: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
NASB.13: For the land of my people [in which] thorns [and] briars shall come up; Yea, for all the joyful houses [and for] the jubilant city.
NASB.14: Because the palace has been abandoned, the populated city forsaken. Hill and watch-tower have become caves forever, A delight for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks;
NASB.15: Until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high, And the wilderness becomes a fertile field, And the fertile field is considered as a forest.
NASB.16: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness And righteousness will abide in the fertile field.
NASB.17: And the work of righteousness will be peace, And the service of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
NASB.18: Then my people will live in a peaceful habitation, And in secure dwellings and in undisturbed resting places;
NASB.19: And it will hail when the forest comes down, And the city will be utterly laid low.
NASB.20: How blessed will you be, you who sow beside all waters, Who let out freely the ox and the donkey.

ESV.1: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule in justice.
ESV.2: Each will be like a hiding place from the wind, a shelter from the storm, like streams of water in a dry place, like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.
ESV.3: Then the eyes of those who see will not be closed, and the ears of those who hear will give attention.
ESV.4: The heart of the hasty will understand and know, and the tongue of the stammerers will hasten to speak distinctly.
ESV.5: The fool will no more be called noble, nor the scoundrel said to be honorable.
ESV.6: For the fool speaks folly, and his heart is busy with iniquity, to practice ungodliness, to utter error concerning the LORD, to leave the craving of the hungry unsatisfied, and to deprive the thirsty of drink.
ESV.7: As for the scoundrel — his devices are evil; he plans wicked schemes to ruin the poor with lying words, even when the plea of the needy is right.
ESV.8: But he who is noble plans noble things, and on noble things he stands.
ESV.9: Rise up, you women who are at ease, hear my voice; you complacent daughters, give ear to my speech.
ESV.10: In little more than a year you will shudder, you complacent women; for the grape harvest fails, the fruit harvest will not come.
ESV.11: Tremble, you women who are at ease, shudder, you complacent ones; strip, and make yourselves bare, and tie sackcloth around your waist.
ESV.12: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
ESV.13: for the soil of my people growing up in thorns and briers, yes, for all the joyous houses in the exultant city.
ESV.14: For the palace is forsaken, the populous city deserted; the hill and the watchtower will become dens forever, a joy of wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;
ESV.15: until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is deemed a forest.
ESV.16: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness abide in the fruitful field.
ESV.17: And the effect of righteousness will be peace, and the result of righteousness, quietness and trust  forever.
ESV.18: My people will abide in a peaceful habitation, in secure dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
ESV.19: And it will hail when the forest falls down, and the city will be utterly laid low.
ESV.20: Happy are you who sow beside all waters, who let the feet of the ox and the donkey range free.

NLT.1:
Look, a righteous king is coming!
And honest princes will rule under him.
NLT.2:
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind
and a refuge from the storm,
like streams of water in the desert
and the shadow of a great rock in a parched land.
NLT.3:
Then everyone who has eyes will be able to see the truth,
and everyone who has ears will be able to hear it.
NLT.4:
Even the hotheads will be full of sense and understanding.
Those who stammer will speak out plainly.
NLT.5:
In that day ungodly fools will not be heroes.
Scoundrels will not be respected.
NLT.6:
For fools speak foolishness
and make evil plans.
They practice ungodliness
and spread false teachings about the LORD.
They deprive the hungry of food
and give no water to the thirsty.
NLT.7:
The smooth tricks of scoundrels are evil.
They plot crooked schemes.
They lie to convict the poor,
even when the cause of the poor is just.
NLT.8:
But generous people plan to do what is generous,
and they stand firm in their generosity.
NLT.9:
Listen, you women who lie around in ease.
Listen to me, you who are so smug.
NLT.10:
In a short time — just a little more than a year —
you careless ones will suddenly begin to care.
For your fruit crops will fail,
and the harvest will never take place.
NLT.11:
Tremble, you women of ease;
throw off your complacency.
Strip off your pretty clothes,
and put on burlap to show your grief.
NLT.12:
Beat your breasts in sorrow for your bountiful farms
and your fruitful grapevines.
NLT.13:
For your land will be overgrown with thorns and briers.
Your joyful homes and happy towns will be gone.
NLT.14:
The palace and the city will be deserted,
and busy towns will be empty.
Wild donkeys will frolic and flocks will graze
in the empty forts and watchtowers
NLT.15:
until at last the Spirit is poured out
on us from heaven.
Then the wilderness will become a fertile field,
and the fertile field will yield bountiful crops.
NLT.16:
Justice will rule in the wilderness
and righteousness in the fertile field.
NLT.17:
And this righteousness will bring peace.
Yes, it will bring quietness and confidence forever.
NLT.18:
My people will live in safety, quietly at home.
They will be at rest.
NLT.19:
Even if the forest should be destroyed
and the city torn down,
NLT.20:
the LORD will greatly bless his people.
Wherever they plant seed, bountiful crops will spring up.
Their cattle and donkeys will graze freely.

WEB.1: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.
WEB.2: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
WEB.3: The eyes of those who see will not be dim, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
WEB.4: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.
WEB.5: The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.
WEB.6: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice profanity, and to utter error against Yahweh, To make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
WEB.7: The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked devices to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.
WEB.8: But the noble devises noble things; and he will continue in noble things.

WEB.12: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.

WEB.14: For the palace will be forsaken. The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;
WEB.15: Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
WEB.16: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.
WEB.17: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
WEB.18: My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
WEB.19: Though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.
WEB.20: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.

AMP.1:
Behold, a King will reign in righteousness,
And princes will rule with justice.
AMP.2:
Each [one of them] will be like a hiding place from the wind
And a shelter from the storm,
Like streams of water in a dry land,
Like the shade of a huge rock in a parched and weary land [to those who turn to them].
AMP.3:
Then the eyes of those who see will not be blinded,
And the ears of those who hear will listen attentively.
AMP.4:
The heart (mind) of those who act impulsively will discern the truth,
And the tongue of the stammerers will hurry to speak clearly.
AMP.5:
The fool (the good-for-nothing) will no longer be called noble,
Nor the rogue said to be generous.
AMP.6:
For the fool speaks nonsense,
And his heart (mind) plans wickedness:
To practice ungodliness and to speak error concerning the LORD,
To keep the craving of the hungry unsatisfied
And to deprive the thirsty of drink.
AMP.7:
As for the rogue, his weapons are evil;
He conceives wicked plans
To ruin the poor with lies,
Even when the plea of the needy one is just and right.
AMP.8:
But the noble man conceives noble and magnificent things;
And he stands by what is noble and magnificent.
AMP.9:
Rise up, you women who are carefree,
And hear my voice,
You confident and unsuspecting daughters!
Listen to what I am saying.
AMP.10:
In little more than a year
You will tremble [with anxiety], you unsuspecting and complacent women;
For the vintage has ended,
And the harvest will not come.
AMP.11:
Tremble, you women who are carefree;
Tremble with fear, you complacent ones!
Strip, undress and wear sackcloth on your waist [in grief],
AMP.12: Beat your breasts [in mourning] for the beautiful fields, for the fruitful vine,
AMP.13:
For the land of my people growing over with thorns and briars—
Yes, [mourn] for all the houses of joy in the joyous city.
AMP.14:
For the palace has been abandoned, the populated city deserted;
The hill [of the city] and the watchtower have become caves [for wild animals] forever,
A delight for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
AMP.15:
Until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high,
And the wilderness becomes a fertile field,
And the fertile field is valued as a forest.
AMP.16:
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness,
And righteousness will live in the fertile field.
AMP.17:
And the effect of righteousness will be peace,
And the result of righteousness will be quietness and confident trust forever.
AMP.18:
Then my people will live in a peaceful surrounding,
And in secure dwellings and in undisturbed resting places.
AMP.19:
But it will hail, when the forest comes down,
And the [capital] city will fall in utter humiliation.
AMP.20:
Blessed (happy, fortunate) are you who cast your seed upon all waters [ when the river overflows its banks and irrigates the land],
You who allow the ox and the donkey to roam freely.

MSG.1:
But look! A king will rule in the right way,
and his leaders will carry out justice.
MSG.2:
Each one will stand as a shelter from high winds,
provide safe cover in stormy weather.
Each will be cool running water in parched land,
a huge granite outcrop giving shade in the desert.
MSG.3:
Anyone who looks will see,
anyone who listens will hear.
MSG.4:
The impulsive will make sound decisions,
the tongue-tied will speak with eloquence.
MSG.5:
No more will fools become celebrities,
nor crooks be rewarded with fame.
MSG.6:
For fools are fools and that's that,
thinking up new ways to do mischief.
They leave a wake of wrecked lives
and lies about God,
Turning their backs on the homeless hungry,
ignoring those dying of thirst in the streets.
MSG.7:
And the crooks? Underhanded sneaks they are,
inventive in sin and scandal,
Exploiting the poor with scams and lies,
unmoved by the victimized poor.
MSG.8:
But those who are noble make noble plans,
and stand for what is noble.
MSG.9:
Take your stand, indolent women!
Listen to me!
Indulgent, indolent women,
listen closely to what I have to say.
MSG.10:
In just a little over a year from now,
you'll be shaken out of your lazy lives.
The grape harvest will fail,
and there'll be no fruit on the trees.
MSG.11:
Oh tremble, you indolent women.
Get serious, you pampered dolls!
Strip down and discard your silk fineries.
Put on funeral clothes.
MSG.12:
Shed honest tears for the lost harvest,
the failed vintage.
MSG.13:
Weep for my people's gardens and farms
that grow nothing but thistles and thornbushes.
Cry tears, real tears, for the happy homes no longer happy,
the merry city no longer merry.
MSG.14:
The royal palace is deserted,
the bustling city quiet as a morgue,
The emptied parks and playgrounds
taken over by wild animals,
delighted with their new home.
MSG.15:
Yes, weep and grieve until the Spirit is poured
down on us from above
And the badlands desert grows crops
and the fertile fields become forests.
MSG.16:
Justice will move into the badlands desert.
Right will build a home in the fertile field.
MSG.17:
And where there's Right, there'll be Peace
and the progeny of Right: quiet lives and endless trust.
MSG.18:
My people will live in a peaceful neighborhood—
in safe houses, in quiet gardens.
MSG.19:
The forest of your pride will be clear-cut,
the city showing off your power leveled.
MSG.20:
But you will enjoy a blessed life,
planting well-watered fields and gardens,
with your farm animals grazing freely.

NET.1: Look, a king will promote fairness; officials will promote justice.
NET.2: Each of them will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from a rainstorm; like streams of water in a dry region and like the shade of a large cliff in a parched land.
NET.3: Eyes will no longer be blind and ears will be attentive.
NET.4: The mind that acts rashly will possess discernment and the tongue that stutters will speak with ease and clarity.
NET.5: A fool will no longer be called honorable; a deceiver will no longer be called principled.
NET.6: For a fool speaks disgraceful things; his mind plans out sinful deeds. He commits godless deeds and says misleading things about the LORD; he gives the hungry nothing to satisfy their appetite and gives the thirsty nothing to drink.
NET.7: A deceiver’s methods are evil; he dreams up evil plans to ruin the poor with lies, even when the needy are in the right.
NET.8: An honorable man makes honorable plans; his honorable character gives him security.
NET.9: You complacent women, get up and listen to me! You carefree daughters, pay attention to what I say!
NET.10: In a year’s time you carefree ones will shake with fear, for the grape harvest will fail, and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
NET.11: Tremble, you complacent ones! Shake with fear, you carefree ones! Strip off your clothes and expose yourselves — put sackcloth on your waist!
NET.12: Mourn over the field, over the delightful fields and the fruitful vine!
NET.13: Mourn over the land of my people, which is overgrown with thorns and briers, and over all the once-happy houses in the city filled with revelry.
NET.14: For the fortress is neglected; the once-crowded city is abandoned. Hill and watchtower are permanently uninhabited. Wild donkeys love to go there, and flocks graze there.
NET.15: This desolation will continue until new life is poured out on us from heaven. Then the desert will become an orchard and the orchard will be considered a forest.
NET.16: Justice will settle down in the desert and fairness will live in the orchard.
NET.17: Fairness will produce peace and result in lasting security.
NET.18: My people will live in peaceful settlements, in secure homes, and in safe, quiet places.
NET.19: Even if the forest is destroyed and the city is annihilated,
NET.20: you will be blessed, you who plant seed by all the banks of the streams, you who let your ox and donkey graze.

NIV.1:
The Kingdom of Righteousness
See, a king will reign in righteousness
and rulers will rule with justice.
NIV.2:
Each man will be like a shelter from the wind
and a refuge from the storm,
like streams of water in the desert
and the shadow of a great rock in a thirsty land.
NIV.3:
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed,
and the ears of those who hear will listen.
NIV.4:
The mind of the rash will know and understand,
and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.
NIV.5:
No longer will the fool be called noble
nor the scoundrel be highly respected.
NIV.6:
For the fool speaks folly,
his mind is busy with evil:
He practices ungodliness
and spreads error concerning the Lord;
the hungry he leaves empty
and from the thirsty he withholds water.
NIV.7:
The scoundrel’s methods are wicked,
he makes up evil schemes
to destroy the poor with lies,
even when the plea of the needy is just.
NIV.8:
But the noble man makes noble plans,
and by noble deeds he stands.
NIV.9:
The Women of Jerusalem
You women who are so complacent,
rise up and listen to me;
you daughters who feel secure,
hear what I have to say!
NIV.10:
In little more than a year
you who feel secure will tremble;
the grape harvest will fail,
and the harvest of fruit will not come.
NIV.11:
Tremble, you complacent women;
shudder, you daughters who feel secure!
Strip off your clothes,
put sackcloth around your waists.
NIV.12:
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields,
for the fruitful vines
NIV.13:
and for the land of my people,
a land overgrown with thorns and briers—
yes, mourn for all houses of merriment
and for this city of revelry.
NIV.14:
The fortress will be abandoned,
the noisy city deserted;
citadel and watchtower will become a wasteland forever,
the delight of donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
NIV.15:
till the Spirit is poured upon us from on high,
and the desert becomes a fertile field,
and the fertile field seems like a forest.
NIV.16:
Justice will dwell in the desert
and righteousness live in the fertile field.
NIV.17:
The fruit of righteousness will be peace;
the effect of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever.
NIV.18:
My people will live in peaceful dwelling places,
in secure homes,
in undisturbed places of rest.
NIV.19:
Though hail flattens the forest
and the city is leveled completely,
NIV.20:
how blessed you will be,
sowing your seed by every stream,
and letting your cattle and donkeys range free.

A fool will no longer be called noble,

NRSVCE.8:

NRSVCE.9:
Rise up, you women who are at ease, hear my voice;

NRSVCE.10:

NRSVCE.11:
Tremble, you women who are at ease,

NRSVCE.15:
